newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Southern Bank seeks to start futures unit.
newsitem.headline: Southern Bank seeks to start futures unit.

text.p: Southern Bank Bhd is seeking to start broking operations in interest rate, currency and other financial futures trading by the end of the year, the national Bernama news agency reported on Wednesday.
The agency quoted Southern Bank chief executive director Tan Teong Hean as saying the bank had all its systems and people in place to start the operations.
Bank officials were not immediately available to comment on the report.
The Malaysian Monetary Exchange approved the bank as a broker last May.

Discussing the government's newly-proposed 50 ringgit annual credit card service tax due to begin on January 1, 1997, the bank's general manager of group finance Abdul Rahim Mohd Zin said the proposed tax would not have much impact on bank performance.
He said contributions from the credit card division were not substantial to the group's earnings.

For the six months ended June 30, 1996, the group reported net profit of 52.19 million ringgit or 24.5 cents a share on turnover of 318.82 million ringgit. It did not detail divisional contributions in its results statement. -- Kuala Lumpur newsroom
